name: single-channel-fokker-planck
title: Schaff et al. 2016, Tests 3–5 / Figs 4–6: a coupled single channel against direct Fokker–Planck solutions
question:
With a single channel whose opening is coupled to calcium (rate αβ(ρ(0) + 1)), does the hybrid
co-simulation reproduce the probability densities of calcium given by direct, Monte-Carlo-free
solutions of the Fokker–Planck equations? Two regimes: fast diffusion (well mixed, Test 3) and
finite diffusion on coarse grids (Tests 4–5), as in Figs 4–6 of the paper.
hypothesis:
The hybrid samples the same piecewise-deterministic process the Fokker–Planck equations
describe, so its histograms should match them to within sampling noise (reduced χ² ≈ 1). The
paper reports L2 differences of 1–3% of the maximum.
objective:
Dimensionless model: ∂τρ = d·∂²ₓρ + a·δ(x)·ξ − ρ. The channel opens at αβ(ρ(0) + 1) and closes
at α; it starts closed, with ρ = 0.

- **Test 3:** α = β = 1, a = 24, d = 10⁴, 3D cube of side 1 (Δx = 0.1, channel at the centre),
  Δτ = 0.002.
  - Compared: p(ρ̄) at τ = 30.
  - Reference: Eq 4, solved in time and checked against its exact steady state.
  - Ensembles: 10,000 co-sim trials, and the same on native VCell.
- **Test 4:** α = 10, β = 1, a = 20/3, d = 1, two cells with Δx = 2, Δτ = 10⁻⁴.
  - Compared: p(ρᵢ) at τ = 1.
  - Reference: the S2-Text master equation (Eq T2.1) at Δρ = 2.5, 1.2 and 0.6 × 10⁻³, extrapolated
    to Δρ → 0.
  - Ensembles: 12,500 trials.
- **Test 5:** α = 20, β = 0.5, a = 20, d = 50, three cells.
  - Reference: four Δρ, extrapolated as in the paper.
  - Ensembles: 12,500 trials at Δτ = 10⁻⁴.

Densities are 20-bin histograms on [0, ρ_max(i)] (40 bins on [0, 24] for Test 3), compared with the
reference averaged over the same bins. Reported: the relative L2 (RMS over bins / reference
maximum), the absolute L2, and the reduced χ² against multinomial sampling noise.
description:
The references are in viva_pde_particle.benchmarks.fokker_planck:
- `fast_steady_state`: the closed form of Eq 4's stationary density,
  p ∝ (a − ρ)^(α−1) ρ^(αβ−1) e^(αβρ);
- `solve_fast`: upwind finite volumes, backward Euler;
- `solve_master`: Eq T2.1, explicit and matrix-free, with `extrapolate`.

The equations come from the paper and its S2 Text. The finite-diffusion model is `imax` equal cells
of width Δx with the channel in cell 0. The co-sim reproduces it with the new `element_volumes`
option of `build_hybrid_document`, which gives every node a full Δx in both the PDE and the
adapter (the node-centred grid would halve the end nodes).

**Deviations:**
- Test 5 runs at Δτ = 10⁻⁴, not 2 × 10⁻⁵.
- Tests 4–5 run only the co-simulation: VCell's node-centred mesh has half-volume end nodes, a
  different discrete model from Eq T2.1.
- Test 3's cube is [0, 1]³ instead of [−0.5, 0.5]³ (Smoldyn placement); this is equivalent.

behavior_tests.name: test3-bias-is-first-order-in-dtau
behavior_tests.description:
Offset of the Test 3 mean-bias fit (offset + slope·Δτ over Δτ = 0.008, 0.004, 0.002, 0.001). Zero means the
gap from Eq 4's steady state is a time-discretization error that vanishes as Δτ → 0.

provenance.note: A first-order scheme has no Δτ-independent bias. The bound is about 3.7 SE (SE ≈ 0.027%).

conclusion:
Results (results/metrics.json, 2026-10-05; relative L2 = RMS over bins / reference maximum):

| test | solver, trials | rel. L2 | sampling noise | reduced χ² | paper |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3 (d = 10⁴), ρ̄ at τ = 30 | co-sim, 10,000 | 0.58% | 0.30% | 2.48 | abs. L2 0.0137 (ours 0.021) |
| 3 | native VCell, 10,000 | 0.58% | 0.30% | 1.82 | |
| 4 (d = 1), ρ(x₀) / ρ(x₁) at τ = 1 | co-sim, 12,500 | 1.0% / 1.6% | 1.5% / 1.7% | 0.54 / 0.80 | 1.9% / 3.3% |
| 5 (d = 50), ρ(x₀) / ρ(x₁) / ρ(x₂) | co-sim, 12,500 | 0.9% / 1.2% / 1.4% | ≈ 1.4% | 0.80 / 0.89 / 0.86 | 1.3% / 1.3% / 1.5% |

- **Finite diffusion (Tests 4–5):** the co-simulation matches the functional Fokker–Planck solutions to within
  sampling noise in every cell (reduced χ² 0.54–0.89), with smaller differences than the paper reports.
  - Extrapolating the reference to Δρ → 0 matters: it shifts the Test 5 reference by about 4% of its maximum and
    Test 4's cell 1 by 1.7%. These are the size of the discrepancies the paper attributes to under-resolved
    Δρ.
- **Fast diffusion (Test 3):** the reference itself is exact. Eq 4 at τ = 30 agrees with its closed-form steady
  state to 0.03%.
  - Both hybrid solvers differ from it by the same 0.58%, about twice the sampling noise. Native VCell's
    reduced χ² (1.82) sits just under the threshold, and the co-sim's (2.48) just over it.
  - Since the two solvers share the same small bias, it belongs to the spatial hybrid at Δτ = 0.002, not to the
    co-simulation.
- **Δτ check (2026-10-08; `dtau` stage, viz/dtau.html):** the Test 3 gap is a first-order time-discretization
  error.
  - 4,000 co-sim trials per Δτ, each sampled at τ = 10, 15, …, 30 (stationary; lag-5 correlation ≈ 0.01).
    SEs are bootstrapped over trials.

    | Δτ | mean bias | SD bias | reduced χ² |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | 0.008 | −0.45% ± 0.03% | +4.4% ± 1.0% | 28.0 |
    | 0.004 | −0.25% ± 0.03% | +2.1% ± 1.0% | 10.6 |
    | 0.002 | −0.12% ± 0.03% | +1.9% ± 1.1% | 2.28 |
    | 0.001 | −0.12% ± 0.03% | +3.6% ± 1.9% | 2.74 |

  - **Mean:** the fit offset + slope·Δτ gives a slope of −0.51 ± 0.06 (−0.10% at Δτ = 0.002) and an offset of
    −0.04% ± 0.03%, consistent with zero (reduced χ² 0.71). Native VCell at Δτ = 0.002 (−0.10% ± 0.04%)
    matches the slope's prediction.
  - **SD:** only Δτ = 0.008 is clearly off. The others are within about 2σ. The skewed density (∝ e^ρ) makes
    the SD's sampling error 2–4× the normal-theory value.
  - The reduced χ² stays above 2 down to Δτ = 0.001. With 20,000 samples, the histogram resolves a 0.1% shift
    of a density that is steep near ρ = a.
